document.title: Pakistan Counterterrorism: Ambassador's Meeting with [Excised] on State Sponsor Designation (Islama 001054)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Secret] The Embassy raises the HUA-bin Laden-Taliban triangle with a Pakistani official. Both bin Laden and HUA have sanctuary in Afghanistan and Khost camps, and the U.S. fears a link-up with serious consequences. The official says HUA is under enough control and Pakistan will not allow bin Laden to use its territory.

events.description: US Ambassador and Army Attache met a Pakistani official (name excised) on possible state sponsor of terrorism designation, delivering talking points and raising HUA movement to Afghanistan and Taliban refuge for bin Ladin.
US Ambassador Simons and Army Attache met an excised Pakistani official, delivering talking points on possible state sponsor of terrorism designation and concerns over HUA and bin Ladin.
Taliban confirmed they were giving refuge to Usama bin Ladin in territory they control.
Planned US visit to two HUA camps in question; Taliban requested delay until after Eid-ul-Fitr.
Pakistani official denied ISI operating outside government control, said HUA under scrutiny for over a year, and pledged Pakistan would not allow its territory to be used by bin Ladin.

key_claims: The Taliban confirmed they were giving refuge to Usama bin Ladin in territory they controlled.
US officials were concerned HUA militant training was relocating from camps in Pakistan/Azad Kashmir to Afghanistan.
The US feared a linkup between HUA, an organization Pakistan supported, and bin Ladin.
The Taliban asked to delay a US visit to two camps until after Eid-ul-Fitr, raising suspicion sites would be cleaned.
A Pakistani official denied ISI was operating outside government control or via rogue elements, claiming HUA had been under strong scrutiny for over a year.
Pakistan pledged not to allow its territory to be used by bin Ladin.
